about.title: Sacramento Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Traffic in Sacramento funnels through a few heavy corridors: US-50 and SR-99 carry commuters in and out of downtown, while Fruitridge Road and Florin Road handle much of the south-side cross traffic. Those four routes appear most often in the county's public collision records. In 2025, the city logged 3,388 injury collisions, with 4,907 people hurt and 48 lives lost. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. account for a noticeable share of those reports. If you were one of the people injured, the paperwork, phone calls, and medical bills tend to arrive faster than answers. LawProactive exists to close that gap. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that pairs you with an independent Sacramento-area personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, but claims involving a government vehicle or agency can carry a six-month notice deadline, so an early conversation matters.

items.title: Deadlines Get Handled Early
items.desc: California's two-year filing window shrinks to as little as six months when a city, county, or state agency is involved. The attorney you are matched with can sort out which clock applies before it becomes a problem.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Close the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and our matching service is free. You can get real guidance without writing a check up front.

items.question: I was hit near the US-50 and SR-99 interchange. Does it matter where the crash happened?
items.answer: Location can matter more than people expect. If road conditions, signage, or a government-owned vehicle played a role, a claim against a public entity may require notice within six months rather than two years. An attorney can review the police report and determine early on whether that shorter deadline applies to your Sacramento crash.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have talked with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you. In the meantime, keep photos, medical records, repair estimates, and any witness contact information in one place.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected with a Sacramento car accident attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorney we connect you with works on a contingency basis, so there is no legal fee unless your case results in a recovery.
